title: mod_watchdog's worker loop reuses a pool it destroyed
live_proof: this corpus pins the allocator, not httpd; the fixture reproduces the call sequence rather than a shipped tree, and says so instead of asserting liveness
object: the per-iteration pool itself -- the handle, not an object inside it
lifetime_ender: apr_pool_destroy, which returns the pool's nodes to the allocator's size-bucketed free list (apr_pools.c:1014 -> :414), never to malloc
shape: stale allocator handle / reuse / allocation through the dead handle
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator: apr_pools.c is upstream's file at the 1.7.4 pin through the port's two patches (freestanding includes, node lifetime hooks); wd_worker's loop, its callbacks and its threading are reduced
distinguishing: in the other corpora the dangling pointer names an object; here it names the allocator, and because the allocator recycles its own control structure the stale handle is silently rebound to a live pool
layer_note: the default APR_ALLOCATOR_MAX_FREE_UNLIMITED frees no nodes at all, so no free() occurs on this path; the port's hooks therefore sit on APR's own free-list transitions, where the reuse happens

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm allocates through the destroyed pool's handle after the allocator has reissued its node; the fixed arm cleared the handle and takes a fresh pool
native-fix-differential.note: pool_struct_reissued is 1 in BOTH arms by design -- the reissue belongs to the allocator, and the arms differ only in whether the consumer still holds the handle

spatial.oracle: the sequence completes: report.completed == 1, no fault, the case marker printed
spatial.role: control for sublet: same binary and guest, one difference. A node keeps the alias it was carved with, so the stale handle names the next pool's storage and apr_palloc through it succeeds

sublet.oracle: fault at the labelled read probe apr_defect_read, and nowhere else: exactly one fault, pc equal to the address the run's own marker published
sublet.note: the probe is the first read through the handle after apr_pool_destroy; the CHECK that the same node came back as the other pool runs before the marker, so the marker's presence is itself evidence that reuse happened

poisoncap-spatial.requires: no CheriBSD or PoisonCap build of APR exists; the port is a compilation census

poisoncap-protected.requires: no CheriBSD or PoisonCap build of APR exists; the port is a compilation census

native-detect.requires: the nodes never reach malloc, so ASan has no event; Valgrind with APR's own annotations is the arm that could discriminate

status: native pair run 2026-09-20 and again 2026-09-21 through the port, both arms as expected. spatial and sublet run in QEMU 2026-09-21: spatial completes (nodes=3, node_reuses=1), sublet faults at apr_defect_read with cause=24 at the published address; negative control fires both oracles; 31 of 32 repetitions returned a result, the one stall a pre-login boot flake. See results/20260921-qemu/. No poisoncap arm: no CheriBSD build of APR exists
note: other_pool_corrupted is 0 and stays 0: the fixture shows allocation proceeding through the stale handle into another arena, not that existing bytes were overwritten, which depends on sizes and ordering. Upstream reports crashes; this records the step before them
